newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Airlines, union talks in holding pattern.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines, union talks in holding pattern.

text.p: Talks in Vancouver between Canadian Airlines Corp and its six unions were on hold early Tuesday as company executives attempted to hammer out a collective agreement with the Canadian Union of Public Employees, which represents its flight attendants.
CUPE, which has 2,700 members at Canadian, was the only one of the unions which had not agreed earlier this year on a deal to to make labor concessions aimed at cutting costs by 17 percent.

Neville Hamilton, spokesman for the International Association of Machinists, said the company's unions had decided to postpone talks with Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson on the company's survival plan late Monday until a tentative labor agreement was struck by CUPE and Canadian.

Canadian, which said it could face financial failure early next year if its plan was not implemented, proposes cutting employee wages by 10 percent, restructuring its route network and reducing fees paid to 33-percent owner AMR Corp by C$48 million per year.
Management and union leaders have been holed up in a Vancouver hotel for the past two days for intense discussions on the plan and CUPE contract.

"They really were in a dreadful situation -- they were meeting mediation commissioner at one end of the hall and running down to the other end of the hall to talk about giving up another 10 percent," Hamilton said.
The flight attendants in September voted in favor of giving their bargaining committee a strike mandate. The previous contract expired at the end of 1995.
Hamilton said it was unclear when talks between Benson and all Canadian's unions, aimed at reaching an agreement on terms of the ailing carrier's life-support plan, would resume.
"Discussions are still ongoing," said a Canadian spokeswoman. "As soon as we have something to report, we'll report it."
